method: Evidence-first catalog using official and primary government sources. Each entry states what the source establishes and its limitations.

records.title: 2020 Electoral College Results
records.establishes: The official Electoral College result recorded 306 electoral votes for Joseph R. Biden Jr. and 232 for Donald J. Trump, with 270 required for a majority.
records.limitations: This record reports the official Electoral College result; by itself it does not resolve every separate allegation or legal argument raised about the election process.

records.title: Congressional Record — Joint Session and Arizona Electoral Vote Objection
records.establishes: Representative Paul Gosar and Senator Ted Cruz submitted a written objection to Arizona's electoral votes. The House and Senate withdrew to consider it separately; after reconvening, the objection was not sustained.
records.limitations: The Congressional Record establishes the official proceedings and statements made in Congress; statements by individual members are not automatically established facts merely because they appear in the record.

records.title: Senate Vote on Arizona Electoral Vote Objection
records.establishes: The Senate rejected the Arizona electoral vote objection by 93 votes to 6.
records.limitations: The vote establishes the Senate's disposition of the objection; it does not by itself adjudicate every factual allegation discussed during debate.

records.title: House Vote on Arizona Electoral Vote Objection
records.originator: U.S. House of Representatives / Government Publishing Office
records.establishes: The House rejected the Arizona electoral vote objection, 303 nays to 121 yeas, with 7 not voting.
records.limitations: The roll call establishes how members voted on the objection, not the truth or falsity of every assertion made during debate.

records.title: Federal Agencies Identified Some Threats Before January 6
records.establishes: GAO found that all 10 federal agencies it reviewed identified potential threats of violence before January 6; the FBI and Capitol Police identified credible threats. GAO also found shortcomings in processing or sharing some threat information.
records.limitations: This is a later government investigative finding rather than a contemporaneous operational record. GAO stated that it did not review certain threat information subject to ongoing investigations or prosecutions.

records.title: Federal Agencies' Use of Open Source Data Prior to January 6
records.establishes: GAO found that all 10 selected agencies were aware of open-source information about planned January 6 events and seven were aware of potential violence planned for that day. The report documents threat information agencies obtained and shared before the attack.
records.limitations: Open-source threat information can establish what agencies received or observed but does not, without corroboration, establish that every online threat was genuine, operational, or carried out.

records.title: Select Committee Final Report and Supporting Materials
records.originator: U.S. House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack / Government Publishing Office
records.establishes: The official collection preserves the Select Committee's final report and supporting materials, including transcripts, court documents, hearing videos, exhibits and other documents used in its investigation. The report states the Committee's findings concerning the causes and circumstances of January 6 and related efforts concerning the 2020 election.
records.limitations: The Committee's conclusions are congressional investigative findings, not criminal convictions or judicial findings. Individual supporting materials should be evaluated according to their own provenance and evidentiary context.

records.title: Bipartisan Senate Investigation of Security, Planning and Response Failures
records.originator: U.S. Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee and Senate Rules Committee
records.establishes: The bipartisan Senate investigation identified failures in intelligence, Capitol Police preparedness, emergency processes and the National Guard response that contributed to the Capitol's vulnerability and delayed the response on January 6.
records.limitations: This is a congressional investigative finding focused substantially on security planning and response. It does not adjudicate individual criminal liability and should not be treated as a judicial determination.

records.title: DOJ Status of Federal Prosecutions Related to January 6
records.originator: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia
records.establishes: The Justice Department's status report provides aggregate federal prosecution information for criminal cases arising from January 6, including numbers charged and categories of alleged offenses.
records.limitations: A charge is an allegation, not a conviction. Aggregate prosecution statistics do not establish the guilt of any particular defendant, and case outcomes must be checked individually. The figures are a historical snapshot and may be affected by later judicial or executive developments.

records.title: Fischer v. United States — DOJ Case Impact Fact Sheet
records.originator: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia
records.establishes: Following the Supreme Court's Fischer decision concerning 18 U.S.C. § 1512(c)(2), DOJ reported that most January 6 defendants had not been charged with or convicted under that provision and that every potentially affected defendant also faced other charges.
records.limitations: This DOJ fact sheet describes the government's assessment of the decision's immediate case impact. The Supreme Court opinion itself controls the legal interpretation, and individual case outcomes require review of their own records.
